subject: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
parts:
Hi,

  I am sending data frames in JSON format to the browser client.

  Usually a data frame is transferred as an JSON object of arrays.

  In the special case where there is only one row, the JSON is an object of primitives

This seems to be the default behaviour of TOJSONIO::toJSON

> library(RJSONIO)
> d=data.frame(a=1:2,b=letters[3:4])
> cat(toJSON(d[1,]))
{
 "a": 1,
"b": "c" 
}
> cat(toJSON(d))
{
 "a": [ 1, 2 ],
"b": [ "c", "d" ] 
}

This transformation is equivalent to the 'drop'=T argument to the `[` operator, but 

I have addressed this on the server side using a function:

    forceTableVector = function(table) {
      lapply(as.list(table),as.list)
    }

But toJSON has an argument to do this:

asIs:
a logical value that, if TRUE causes R vectors of length 1 to be represented as arrays in JSON, but if FALSE to be represented as scalars, where appropriate (i.e. not the top level of the JSON content). This avoids having to explicitly mark sub-elements in an R object as being of class AsIs.

> cat(toJSON(d[1,],asIs=T))
{
 "a": [ 1 ],
"b": [ "c" ] 
}

But perhaps shiny could make this transformation the default (especially while it's still beta!)

Note that the asIS `I()` function does not help here:

> cat(toJSON(I(d[1,])))
{
 "a": 1,
"b": "c" 
}

But an alternative formulation of the forceTable function is suggested by this:

> cat(toJSON(lapply(d[1,],I)))
{
 "a": [ 1 ],
"b": [ "c" ] 
}

-Alex Brown

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
parts: Sorry Alex, didn't mean to ignore this one. I was pretty sure this was going to be a problem but I didn't have a great solution. I don't love the idea of *everything* being an array all the time, but at the same time it is pretty surprising/insane for the type to change based on how many rows are in the data frame. I'm not sure how flexible RJSONIO is, but it would be ideal if we could treat data frames, matrices, etc. different than atomic vectors and lists.

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Re: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
parts:
The final version - wrapping the data frame list elements with I() is much faster than the list conversion function I supplied at the top.

Automatic strength reduction is one of my least favorite features of R - it causes constant pain.

-Alex.
